confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors rest on 2026 French price reports: Numbeo-based regional draft-beer and cappuccino figures, a crowdsourced Aix-en-Provence cost-of-living page (inexpensive meal and two-person three-course meal), and Paris and Bordeaux cocktail and wine-by-the-glass estimates. Aix-specific cocktail, wine and beer prices are inferred from those comparables and the local beer-to-wine relationship, so they are less certain than the restaurant anchors. Euro figures were converted at an assumed EUR/USD of about 1.15 that I did not verify by search. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge and July festival-season context (the Festival d'Aix); I did not check live booking pages or current listings. FX: the only RBA observation I could retrieve is the 20 March 2026 USD rate (0.7088) from the rba.gov.au exchange-rates page snippet. That is about seven months before the generation date, I could not confirm it is the latest published observation, and a search for an October 2026 rate returned nothing current.
comparable_city_reasoning: Aix-en-Provence is a mid-sized French university and tourist city. Its food and drink prices are benchmarked to French regional averages and to Paris and Bordeaux comparables, with Aix-specific cost-of-living figures where available. Accommodation is estimated from comparable mid-sized Provençal tourist towns in peak summer season.
